problem: It says an emergency stop is a control that 'pauses the app and lifts the display'. Software cannot lift the display; a button, voice command or gesture cannot physically move the headset. A student will read this as a mechanical action and be confused about what the stop actually does.
fix: An emergency stop is a visible button, voice command or hand gesture that pauses the app at once and shows a message asking the user to stop moving and remove the headset. The physical action of taking the headset off is done by the user or the spotter, not by the app.

problem: 'Guardian boundary' is one vendor's product name used as if it were the general term. Some syllabi use chaperone boundary or safety boundary, and readers meeting the generic idea for the first time may think only one brand has it.
fix: A safety boundary (some systems call it a guardian or chaperone) shows walls or a grid when the user nears the edge.
